title: Like a GIF For Your Yard
description: Simulate Conway's Game of Life on a 100x100 grid of lights.
writeup:
## Approach

This is a classic cellular automaton (Game of Life). Each step, a light stays on with 2–3 neighbors, turns on with exactly 3, and turns off otherwise. Using a set of active cells and only checking their neighborhoods makes each step efficient.

## Part 1

Run the simulation for 100 steps on the initial grid and count the lights that are on.

## Part 2

Same simulation, but the four corner lights are stuck on — they're forced on after every step regardless of the rules. This slightly increases the final count since corners can seed additional growth.
